title: Introduction to Cryptography
subtitle: Goals of cryptography: confidentiality, integrity, authenticity

content.text: Cryptography provides four security properties: confidentiality (data is secret), integrity (data is not modified), authentication (identity is verified), and non-repudiation (actions cannot be denied).

content.definition: The original, readable data before encryption.
The encrypted, unreadable version of data produced by an encryption algorithm.
A secret value used by a cryptographic algorithm. The security of the system depends on the key, not the algorithm.

content.code:
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import hashes
from cryptography.hazmat.backends import default_backend
import os

# Hash a message
digest = hashes.Hash(hashes.SHA256(), backend=default_backend())
digest.update(b"Hello, cryptography!")
hash_value = digest.finalize()
print(hash_value.hex())

content.text: Kerckhoff's principle: a system should be secure even if everything about it except the key is public knowledge.

questions.question: What does confidentiality mean in cryptography?
options: Only authorised parties can read the data
questions.explanation: Confidentiality ensures that data is accessible only to those authorised to read it.

faq.q: Is secrecy of the algorithm important?
faq.a: No. Per Kerckhoff's principle, security must rely on the key, not on keeping the algorithm secret. Open algorithms are stronger because they are peer-reviewed.
